coordinates.note: No fetched source gives the longitude of Pampa La Bola. The latitude (22.9 deg S, one decimal) is from the 2023 SWGO site paper; the longitude (67.7875 deg W) is borrowed from the sourced ACT position on Cerro Toco (src:c2-cmb-act-receiver), because the same paper says the SWGO sites are "near astronomical observatories at Cerro Toco and ALMA in the Chajnantor plateau" and the 2014 concession names "the area called Pampa La Bola, Llano de Chajnantor" as part of the same park. The point is a regional anchor with 25 km precision, not a surveyed position. Earlier SWGO papers print other latitudes for the same site (22.56 S in arXiv:2111.13158, 22.25 S in arXiv:2309.04577), most likely different notations; the discrepancy is logged.

name: SWGO site, Pampa La Bola
notes: Coordinates are a regional anchor, not a survey: see the coordinates note.
A proposed site: the array is not built; the SWGO Pathfinder (SWGO-PF) is described in the 2025 science paper as the first activity planned there.

summary.plain: A high, flat desert plateau in northern Chile, inside the Atacama Astronomical Park, chosen as the home of the planned SWGO gamma-ray observatory.
summary.technical: Pampa La Bola, a plateau at 4770 m in the Atacama Astronomical Park (Calama commune, near San Pedro de Atacama), selected in 2024 as the site of SWGO; no detector has been built at the site yet.
